findings.claim: The contract 'every folder under .okf/prototypes/ has a README.md' does not say whether it means only the direct child folders or every folder at any depth. Read literally it is recursive, so any prototype holding code in a subfolder (src/, data/) would fail kmctl check, and the planned fixtures (one flat passing, one flat failing) would not catch it. State that only direct children of .okf/prototypes/ are prototypes, and add a passing fixture with a nested folder that has no README.md.

Round 1: 'every folder under .okf/prototypes/' read as recursive. The plan now checks only folders directly under .okf/prototypes/, says nested folders (src/, results/) are not prototypes, and adds a fixture with a nested folder that has no README.md.

The kmctl check help still says it only checks that docs/ and .okf/ indexes agree with their folders. It does not mention the new prototype README.md check, and that help is the text an agent reads before it runs the command. The first line of the checks.py module docstring has the same gap.

entries.change: The kmctl check help now says it also checks that each prototype folder has a README.md.
The module docstring first line names the prototype README check.
